subject: MAP Draft: Data handling & compliance - MediApp Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@mediapp.com>
Cc: Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@mediapp.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP Draft: Data handling & compliance - MediApp Health

Hi Sara / Michael,

Thanks again for the call this morning - great to hear more about MediApp's roadmap and the PHI-sensitive workflows you mentioned. Per our discussion, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the data-handling & compliance milestone we agreed to prioritize. Key points called out in the doc and summarized below: 

MAP milestone: Data handling & compliance (scope)
- Retention: default request/response logs retained for 90 days; optional extended audit export to customer S3 for 7 years (if requested).
- Logging & audit trails: immutable request logs including timestamp, model version, token counts, request metadata. Optional body redaction to avoid storing PII/PHI.
- PHI/PII constraints: by-default we do not perform automated PHI extraction; recommend customer-side redaction. For covered workflows, we offer isolated Dedicated capacity or Private deployment to meet your compliance needs.
- Encryption & key management: customer-managed keys (KMS) for private deployments; hosted API supports envelope encryption and bring-your-own-KMS for enterprise tiers.
- Responsibilities (first pass):
  - MediApp: provide sample dataset and redaction rules; confirm required retention period and legal hold needs.
  - Redwood: provide SOC 2 evidence, sample audit logs, and a technical runbook for exporting logs to your S3.
  - Legal (both): align on data processing addendum (DPA) and any PHI-specific addendum.
- Target close date for this milestone: 2026-04-30 (aligns with your Q2 pilot start).
- Dependencies / blockers: completed SOC 2 evidence review, legal signoff on DPA, network connectivity test to your VPC / S3 for exports.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal: I’ll loop in our security engineering team with the MAP doc and draft Security Q&A responses (attached).
2) Action: Can you confirm the retention period you need (90 days vs 7 years) and whether MediApp requires us to store raw request bodies?
3) Schedule: Let’s book a 45-min follow-up next week to walk through SOC 2 artifacts and the export runbook.

Attaching: MediApp_MAP_v1.1.pdf (MAP draft), Security_QA_Responses.xlsx (initial answers).

Thanks - Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@mediapp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@mediapp.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP Draft: Data handling & compliance - MediApp Health

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful and mirrors what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: Our clinical compliance team needs logs retained for at least 3 years for auditability. That said, we prefer not to keep raw request bodies containing PHI longer than 90 days unless absolutely necessary. 
- Redaction: We can provide redaction rules for patient identifiers, but we need confirmation that redaction can happen before any persistent storage on Redwood's side. 
- Deployment: For the pilot, we'd like to start on Redwood Dedicated (isolated GPU pool) and then evaluate Private for production.

Action items for you: please confirm if the export-to-S3 option supports incremental exports (daily) and whether we can set a legal hold on specific records. Also, can you add our compliance lead (I’ll introduce in the next thread) to the follow-up?

Appreciate it - Sara

Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP Draft: Data handling & compliance - MediApp Health

Hi Sara / team - looping in with a few technical confirmations from Redwood infra/security: 

- Redaction before storage: We support request-body redaction at the proxy edge. Redaction rules can be customer-supplied (regex-based) and applied in-line so that raw PHI is never persisted.
- Retention & legal hold: Audit logs (metadata + redaction markers) are retained 90 days by default on hosted; we can export daily incremental batches to your S3 for longer retention (configurable schedule). Legal hold is supported: we tag and retain specific records indefinitely in your encrypted export bucket until release.
- Storage of embeddings / model outputs: by default we do not store embeddings; if you opt-in for caching, we can configure TTLs (default 7 days for cache) and separate the storage so customer controls longer-term retention.
- Audit trail detail: exported logs include timestamp, model version, request-id, route, token counts, and a redaction marker; request bodies are only included if customer explicitly enables body export.
- PHI handling: for Dedicated/Private we can enable stricter controls (no outbound internet, customer-managed KMS, and disabled analytics) to meet HIPAA-like expectations.

I'll add these notes to the Security_QA_Responses.xlsx and attach updated excerpts. Marissa - happy to join the follow-up call to walk through the export runbook.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@mediapp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP Draft: Data handling & compliance - MediApp Health

Thanks everyone - that addresses the bulk of our concerns. Confirming next steps from MediApp side:

- I’ll introduce our compliance lead (Lena Park) in the next thread - she’ll review the MAP and the Security_QA sheet.
- We prefer daily incremental exports to S3 with a 3-year retention policy; we will request legal hold capability during audit windows.
- We agree to start pilot on Dedicated; pilot target start remains 2026-05-04.

From Redwood: please update the MAP with:
- explicit note that redaction can occur at edge before storage;
- export schedule options (daily/weekly) and a short runbook for the S3 export process;
- confirmation of legal-hold tag support and steps to request release.

If you can send an updated MAP and Security Q&A by end of day Friday (2026-03-20), I’ll aim to have our compliance lead review on Monday. Looking forward to the follow-up call - please propose 2x 45-min time slots next week.

Best,
Sara
